figures.caption: Figure 1. Schematic overview of modeling approaches and measurable quantities across scales in polymer-based battery electrolyte systems. Arrows denote information flow among experimental measurements, modeling representations, scale-associated quantities, multiscale complexities, and formulation–processing–structure–property–performance factors.

Figure 2. Diagnostic framework used in this Perspective to classify modeling studies according to modeling objective, modeling basis, degree of process coupling, and characteristic scale or data level.

Figure 3. Distribution of (a) modeling basis and (b) modeling objective and process coupling across scale/data levels in the identified ionogel electrolyte studies, with multilevel studies counted in each applicable category and, in panel b, color and bubble size denoting coupling and study placements, respectively.

Figure 4. Two strategies for transferring and adapting existing materials–processing–microstructure–performance models to polymer-electrolytecontaining composite electrodes: the hard-carbon electrode calendering model adapted from ref 145 under the terms of the Creative Commons Attribution License and the solid-state battery composite electrode model adapted from ref 154 with permission from Elsevier.
